pr_title: fix test flake caused by not waiting for CRD schema update
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind failing-test
/kind flake

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Fixes a flake in some test code. Flake was caused by our check to make sure CRD schema was updated. We would check to see a returned error had special string, but the error message would unconditionally contain the string since we had used within the send value, so we never would actually wait....I'm surprised it did not flake more than it had.

FIxed by no longer sending the special string in with the object, and instead encoding the special string as a custom CEL error message. This is a better way of checking that the new schema is being updated.

review_comments: does switching this from a declarative openapi validation to a CEL rule change the ratcheting logic it is exercising?
is there a way to keep this declarative and still output the message (like making the sentinal uuid an enum or something) ... just trying to minimize the test change

> does switching this from a declarative openapi validation to a CEL rule change the ratcheting logic it is exercising?

This code is not for triggering the validation being tested and not meant to excercise ratcheting logic, this is meant to just observe that the new schema has taken effect, before we continue with testing ratcheting. Since also all objects are net new CREATEs I dont expect ratcheting to take effect for this operation. Even if the object did exist prior, it should be impossible for it to have the ratcheting_sentinel_field which would not be ratcheted.

> is there a way to keep this declarative and still output the message (like making the sentinal uuid an enum or something) ... just trying to minimize the test change

Changed from using CEL error message to using enum, which also includes the cases in its output:

```
"MyCoolCRD.mygroup.example.com \"sentinel-resource\" is invalid: __ratcheting_sentinel_field__: Unsupported value: \"invalid-0\": supported values: \"8c1cc36b-9240-4405-8f25-c1d5878eac0d\""
```
